newsitem.title: USA: Texas Instruments Vice Chairman Mitchell to retire.
newsitem.headline: Texas Instruments Vice Chairman Mitchell to retire.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc. Vice Chairman William Mitchell is to retire at the end of this year, the company said on Monday.
Mitchell, 60, was one of two senior executives widely touted as natural successors to Jerry Junkins, the president and chief executive officer who died of a heart attack in Germany in May.
But Junkins' job instead went to Thomas Engibous, a younger, dark-horse candidate who had previously led the Dallas-based company's semiconductor division.

Engibous said in a statement that Mitchell, who was also a member of Texas Instruments' board of directors, had planned to retire for over a year, although analysts said they suspected he decided to step down after being passed over.

"If you are vice chairman and you share the office of chief executive and somebody underneath you is named CEO, I guess it's time to go," said William J. Milton, an analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman.
Mitchell joined Texas Instruments 35 years ago. In 1993, he was named vice chairman and a member of the newly-created Office of the Chief Executive under Junkins' leadership.

Mitchell is an expert on the defense-electronics side of Texas Instruments' business, which last year accounted for less than 15 percent of total revenues, down from its peak of around 30 percent in the late 1980s.

"Bill's perspective has been an invaluable asset to the management team as we've worked to reposition each of the company's major businesses to better meet the needs of our customers," Engibous said on Monday.
Company officials said Mitchell's retirement had nothing to do with the change in leadership following Junkins' death, and that he was retiring to spend more time with his family.
A successor to Mitchell was not named.
Over the last year, Mitchell served as chairman of the American Electronics Association, a high technology trade organization.
